The **Imjin War** (임진왜란, 1592–1598) was a major conflict between the Japanese forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi and the Korean Joseon dynasty, with support from Ming China. It is also known as the **Japanese invasions of Korea**. ### Key points | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Timeframe** | 1592 – 1598 | | **Main belligerents** | Japan (led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi) vs. Korea (Joseon) and Ming China | | **Causes** | Hideyoshi sought to conquer Korea as a stepping stone to invade Ming China. He also wanted to punish Korea for refusing to provide troops for his planned invasion of China. | | **Major phases** | 1. **First invasion (1592–1593)** – Japanese forces quickly captured Seoul and advanced north. 2. **Ming intervention** – Chinese troops joined the fight, pushing back the Japanese. 3. **Second invasion (1597–1598)** – Japanese attempted a comeback but were defeated. | | **Notable events** | • The **Battle of Hansan Island** (1592) – Admiral Yi Sun-sin’s naval victory using turtle ships.
• The **Siege of Pyongyang** (1593) – Korean and Ming forces recaptured the city.
• The **Battle of Noryang** (1598) – Final naval engagement; Japanese fleet destroyed, marking the end of the war. | | **Outcome** | Japan was forced to withdraw; Korea regained its territory. The war devastated Korea’s population, economy, and infrastructure. It also led to increased Chinese influence over Korea and a shift in regional power dynamics. | | **Legacy** | • The war is remembered in Korea as a period of national resilience and sacrifice.
• Admiral Yi Sun-sin is celebrated as a national hero.
• The conflict influenced later East Asian geopolitics, including the rise of the Qing dynasty and the eventual decline of Japanese power until the 20th century. | ### Why it matters - **Cultural memory**: The Imjin War is a central part of Korean history, taught in schools and commemorated in monuments and literature. - **Military history**: It showcased early modern naval warfare, especially the use of the turtle ship and coordinated land‑naval operations. - **International relations**: The war set the stage for future Sino‑Japanese rivalry and shaped the balance of power in East Asia.
